newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo talking to Union Miniere on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Anglo talking to Union Miniere on Zaire.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday it had held talks with Union Miniere on joint operations to develop Zaire's Kolwezi tailings project, if Anglo's bid for the scheme was successful.
"Anglo and Union Miniere have had discussions with regard to possbly working together should Anglo be successful with this tender," Anglo spokeswoman Glen Finnegan said.
Anglo has put in a tender to retreat the tailings from the copper mine which was shut down after foreign exchange earnings dried up and the mine ran out of spare parts for machinery.
Analysts said if the project went ahead, it could have a significant impact on the price of cobalt -- currently around $20.00/21.00 a pound for cobalt cathodes.
Projected cobalt output was about 6,000 tonnes a year, against world production of 20,000 tonnes.
Belgium's Financieel Economische Tijd newspaper reported last week that the project would involve an investment of between six and nine billion francs.
Zaire's state-owned mining company Gecamines would also be involved in the project, the paper said.
The joint business project would take over the business and premises of purifier KZC, Concentrateur Kolwezi and would produce around 80,000 tonnes of copper in addition to the cobalt over a decade.

A Johannesburg investment analyst, who asked not to be identified, said Anglo was the frontrunner for the tender. Other South African companies like Gencor Ltd, JCI Ltd and Iscor Ltd had also submitted tenders.
The analyst said the project would see the Kolwezi tailings dams being treated while another source of cobalt and copper would be the nearby river, he added.
"You have also got the river because when the dams were full they just threw the stuff in the river," he added.
Anglo said last year it was likely to invest in strife-torn Zaire but would do so with caution.
Analysts see Zaire as one of the richest mineral resource areas in the world but escalating political chaos and corruption has devastated its production of base and precious metals.
